result.title: When "A or B" Is Less Likely than A: Coherent Probabilities for Vision Decision Models
result.summary: Vision decision models answer a multiple-choice question about an image with one probability per option, and software uses them directly. We show that the probabilities depend on how the options are grouped: a merged option "A or B" receives on average 11.5 points less probability than the sum of A and B. This under-additivity appears at every model size from 0.85B to 26B and remains after fine-tuning on labels. We propose CORE, which asks each training question with its options regrouped and trains the answers to all these questions toward one target distribution over the original options, summed into each question's groups. On 1,050 items from seven benchmarks, CORE reduces the total variation distance between the answer to a regrouped question and the original answer summed into the same groups from 14.8 to 5.8 points on the 0.85B model, against 9.4 for the best baseline trained on the same questions. At all five model sizes, CORE reduces this distance without lowering accuracy.

AI.brief_summary: 论文揭示视觉决策模型对选项分组存在概率不一致：「A 或 B」的概率低于 A 与 B 之和，并提出 CORE 通过重新分组选项、训练各组概率汇总回原选项分布来提升一致性，且不降低准确率。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接涉及 VLM 答案概率与决策评价；其分组边缘化一致性可供核查多假设或证据汇总时的概率使用，但未触及内部 latent 状态或推理轨迹。
